entities.summary:
Meretnebty was a queen consort of Egypt during the 5th Dynasty, specifically during the reign of King Sahure (c. 2483 - 2474 BCE), and was named after Two Ladies, a pair of Egyptian goddesses who protected the king. She is known for her role in the royal court and her connection to the worship of the goddess Isis. Meretnebty's life and significance are closely tied to the period of Egyptian history known as the Old Kingdom, during which time the pharaohs built monumental temples and established a complex system of hieroglyphic writing.

She played a key role in the royal family, serving as a consort to King Sahure and later as a regent for her son, King Neferirkare. Her involvement in the royal family and her connections to the goddess Isis make her an important figure in the study of ancient Egyptian history and culture.

Despite the limited information available about her life, Meretnebty's significance can be understood through her role in the Old Kingdom and her connections to the royal family and the goddess Isis.

The worship of Isis continued long after Meretnebty's death, with the cult gaining popularity in the Roman period and remaining an important part of Egyptian culture until the Arab conquest of Egypt in the 7th century CE.
